description.en-US:
Claude Code Bridge for Firefox lets Claude Code use your everyday Firefox. It can open tabs, click, type, read pages, fill forms, take screenshots, and read console and network logs. It works in your real profile, with your logins.

**Setup**

The add-on needs Claude Code and its companion bridge, which you install with Node 20 or newer:

`npx @llyfn/claude-in-firefox install`

Then start a new Claude Code session and ask it to use Firefox.

**What it sends, and where**

Each Claude Code session gets its own Firefox window. Claude can only read and act on the tabs in that window, plus popups opened from them. From those tabs the add-on sends page content (text, page structure, form fields, screenshots, console messages and network requests) and browsing activity (addresses and titles) to the bridge on your computer through Firefox native messaging. The bridge hands them to Claude Code, which sends them to Claude as part of your conversation. The add-on sends nothing to its developer.

**Staying in control**

Every page in a session window shows a "Claude is using this window · Stop" bar. Stop cancels the running action and blocks Claude until you press Resume. Closing the window ends the session.

**Before you use it**

Claude acts as you, with your logged-in sessions, and the add-on blocks no sites. A page can contain text written to steer Claude. Read [Safety](https://github.com/llyfn/claude-in-firefox#safety) before you use it on sites that matter.
